label: c4lf-lines-heavy-s0
target_hash_note: recheck.json carries no target_hash for a record JSON target
scope: record, structure, every annotation's hypothesis, closed form and evidence; no drafts, claims or prose exist for this genome

overall.summary: Every stated number reproduces (coverage, preservation, closed forms, counts, AUCs, probe values, concept scores). Nothing is refuted. Five units are weakened: the quiet-o gate fires without x in the centre on 28% of its firings; the summary's o-threat switch is general for the ramp but not for the cap (still on for 149 of 765 o-threat rows); the pair's 'both raise x's chance with more open lines' fails for open twos through unit 8; o's open singles stop lowering the chance once the gated units floor (direct +0.20); the x-singles-vs-twos gate's hypothesis restates its closed form. Two domain flags (x's open twos lower x's chance through the ramp; o's open singles raise it directly).

ann_54.why: 'o is quiet (few open singles and twos) and x holds the centre, so x is winning' is a game reading the model confirms (gate on where x wins 93.6%, concept AUC 0.95), though x's centre pieces only shift the threshold: 28% of firings have none.

ann_55.why: 'o's line presence lowers x's chance, switched off by an o threat' holds (unit falls with o's singles and twos, off on all 765 o-threat rows), but the unit falls as much with x's own open twos and rises with o's centre pieces, terms the reading does not explain (two-term reading scores 0.66).

ann_56.why: 'x's open twos raise x's chance until about two, then the part adds nothing' is a game reading the model confirms (unit floors at 2 at the typical case, concept AUC 0.94, floor rows win 82.5% vs 58.8%).

ann_57.why: the gate does rise with x's open singles and o's centre pieces and fall with x's centre pieces, but only 39% of its firings have o with two or more centre pieces and 16% have none; the concept scores 0.65 and the game sense of the conjunction is not given.

ann_58.why: the hypothesis is the closed form's largest terms in words (rises with x's singles, falls with x's twos, even-row columns and odd threats); the predicate is accurate (AUC 0.90) but no game reading says why singles minus twos minus even-row playable columns should matter.

ann_59.why: 'x in the centre is good for x; a crowded centre column (either side) is bad' is a game reading the model confirms at the block level (contribution +1.17 at x3/o0, -0.92 at x0/o3, -2.53 at x1/o3; total centre pieces predict the three exits with AUC 0.97).

ann_60.why: unit 8 reads x's open singles against o's centre and lines as stated, but unit 9 is described by its formula, the concept scores 0.61, and the stated 'both raise x's chance with more open lines' fails for open twos through unit 8.

ann_61.why: 'the direct effect is dominated by x's open twos' is a reading the model confirms (R-squared 0.86), but the other six terms are listed as weights without a game reading, and the positive direct weight on o's open singles is unexplained.
